title: Go: Pointers
description: Use pointers to reference and modify values, work with pointer to struct, and understand nil pointers.

steps.title: & and *
steps.description: Declare `x := 42`. Create a pointer `p` to `x` using `&`, print the pointer and dereference it with `*`.
hints: `*p` gets the value at that address.

verification.failureMessage: Create a pointer to x=42, dereference it, and print 42.

steps.title: Pointer to Struct
steps.description: Define a `Person` struct with `Name string`. Create a pointer to a Person instance and access fields via the pointer.

verification.failureMessage: Create a pointer to Person{Name:'Alice'} and print the name.

steps.title: Modify via Pointer
steps.description: Write a function `zero(i *int)` that sets the value pointed to by `i` to 0. Pass an int's address and print the result.
hints: Print x after the call — it should be 0.

verification.failureMessage: Write zero(*int) that sets value to 0, call with x=42, print x.

steps.title: Nil Pointer Check
steps.description: Declare a pointer `var p *int` without initializing it. Check if it's nil and print a message.
hints: A nil pointer has no address assigned.
Since it's nil, print something like `"p is nil"`.

verification.failureMessage: Check if p is nil and print a message.

steps.title: Pointer vs Value
steps.description: Define a `Counter` struct with `Value int`. Write methods `IncrementValue()` (value receiver) and `IncrementPointer()` (pointer receiver), call both, and print differences.
hints: `func (c Counter) IncrementValue() { c.Value++ }` vs `func (c *Counter) IncrementPointer() { c.Value++ }`
Create counter, call both, print Value.

verification.failureMessage: Show that only pointer receiver actually increments the counter.
